utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, may I confirm that you're receiving interpretation, and you can understand the proceedings? And as usual, should you have any problems with that, just let me know. Thank you. Appearances. Mr. McCloskey, you have a full team today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: With me today is Janet Stewart, Nelson Thayer, Kweku Vanderpuye, and Caitlin Chittenden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. And, Mr. Tolimir, self-represented. I note Mr. Gajic is present in the courtroom, one of his legal advisors. We have a two-fold purpose for today's hearing, and I'll deal first with the further appearance, which has been necessitated as a result of the granting of the Prosecution's motion to amend the second indictment. Just briefly by way of history, on the 4th of November, the Prosecution filed their motion to amend the indictment; and on the 9th of December, the Chamber granted the motion in a decision, with reasons to follow, and ordered that the third amended indictment be the operative indictment. The reasons for that decision were filed today. The Trial Chamber has concluded that two of the amendments which were granted involve new charges, for which pleas are required, and specifically that is paragraph 21.15.2, which alleges the execution on or about the 23rd of July, 1995, of approximately 39 Muslim men in Bisina and paragraph 23.1 which alleges the execution and burial on or about 27th July 1995, of three Bosnian leaders from Zepa. As a result, the Trial Chamber is of the opinion that these new charges are relevant to Counts 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 of the indictment, and, therefore, I will be proceeding to enter pleas with respect to these new charges. Mr. Tolimir, can I confirm that you have received the third amended indictment in your own language which includes these new charges? Can you confirm that for me, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] God help us all, everybody in the courtroom, to you, the Presiding Judge, and everybody else, and may God's will be done during this trial. I have received the third amended indictment. I received it on the 15th. Thank you, your health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you then, Mr. Tolimir. I will read out for the record the factual allegations amounting to these new charges unless you are satisfied that you've reviewed the two paragraphs and you waive the reading of those allegations. It's up to you as to whether I should review those here now or whether you will waive the reading of the new charges.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Presiding Judge. I have received it, I've understood it, and I have responded to all the indictments in written form. You have received all my responses, and I don't think I need say more now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: But would you like me to read the substance of the new charges before I take pleas regarding them, or are you waiving that requirement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm waiving that requirement. As I say, I've already responded to all such cumulative charges in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I note that you have waived the requirement for those allegations to be read to you, and, therefore, I would ask you to stand at this point, Mr. Tolimir, and to enter pleas regarding these new charges.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can say that I'm not guilty for what you are charging me with in those new counts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, if -- I will just put this to you. In relation to the new charges applicable to Counts 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already said that I'm not guilty. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. We can enter -- pleas of not guilty have been entered with respect to the relevant counts to the new charges. We note that on the record. That will -- I simply want to remind you, Mr. Tolimir, by virtue of the Rules, of course, it is always open to you at any time to indicate that you wish to enter a change of plea. But you have clearly indicated today your pleas of not guilty. And I wish to remind you that in accordance with the decision which the Chamber has issued, the 30-day limit under Rule 50(C) to file preliminary motions pursuant to Rule 72 in respect of the new charges and that time-period began to run on the 10th of December. So you have that 30-day period to bring preliminary motions in respect of the amended indictment. I will now proceed into the second phase of today's hearing, which is the Status Conference itself. This will be the tenth Status Conference. We had anticipated the last one to have been on the 22nd of October, but as indicated, events have overtaken with the granting of the Prosecution's motion. I believe after the previous Status Conferences everyone is well familiar with our purpose here, and as the matter was to start for trial this week, there is little left in terms of any preparation matters to deal with. However, I did want to raise a couple of matters. In particular, I note that the Prosecution today -- or I received it today has filed a motion relating to protective measures and requesting amendment to the witness list. Mr. McCloskey, I wonder if you could advise if you have any particular remarks to make as a result of that motion with respect to the proposed timing of the trial, if you -- if there's anything in particular you wanted to say regarding the time estimates. If not, it's not a difficulty, but I wondered if you had any updated information you wanted to provide for the purposes of trial scheduling?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At this time we don't anticipate these additions to take any significantly more time than what we've already talked about and the amendments to the -- or the addition to the 65 ter list is our ongoing effort to identify the most relevant documents that may be used at trial, and we will be providing all of these -- these documents have all been provided to the Defence, but we are engaged in making an index where they are all in together by subject matter, by date. So all these most-relevant documents of the last trial and this trial are clearly accessible and to try to reduce the entry of new or unknown documents into the trial. So I think we're getting very close to that at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. Mr. Tolimir, did you have any matters that you wished to raise regarding trial preparations. I believe that the topic has been exhaustively considered in the previous Status Conferences, but if there's any matter you wish to raise at this point regarding trial preparations, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to kindly ask you once again, when it comes to the materials from Popovic, Krstic, Blagojevic, to disclose them to me in a timely manner because even though I have asked this long time ago, the OTP hasn't disclosed them yet. So could you please assist us in ensuring that this motion that we submitted long time ago, in a timely fashion, is abided by. The second thing I would like to ask you is to tell us when we can expect the ruling of the Chamber pursuant to the OTP motion under Rule 92 bis. Thank you. That's all I have, for the secretariat to disclose the aforementioned material and for the ruling of the Trial Chamber to be handed down. That's all I have concerning the preparations. And another matter I want to ask you is to see whether my legal assistants could be granted the appropriate hours of work they need in order to work on a pre-trial brief. Because now as it stands they need to do everything in one month's time, and they need to be paid for their work, not to work pro bono. We filed a motion, and I expect that you can assist as the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. I'll address those points. To begin with, yes, I did -- do recall the issue you raised previously regarding the disclosure of the confidential materials from the trial proceedings in Popovic, Krstic, Blagojevic, and Jokic. I have followed up on that matter, and because of the conditions which were imposed regarding personal information and Rule 70 material, that has been the source of the delay in the disclosure. I am advised, however, that the -- particularly with the Popovic material, it is almost ready to go. We're awaiting, I believe, information from one Defence team. So that should be disclosed to you shortly. And the Registry is, I know, doing their very best with respect to Blagojevic, Jokic, and Krstic material, which they have to review on their own, in light of the fact that the proceedings have been completed. But I'm assured that they have amassed the material, and you should have access to that as well very shortly. So I'm anticipating quite shortly you will have access to all of those materials. As I say, the delay relates to the conditions upon which the confidential material is being released. I'm not in a position to give a precise date as to when the Trial Chamber will deliver the rulings on any of the outstanding motions, including 92 bis, but you can be assured that the Chamber is working very diligently to deliver those decisions as soon as possible, and appreciating the impact they have on the trial proceedings. So they will be delivered -- all of the outstanding motions will be decided in due course, but I'm not in a position to set a dead-line, if you will, as to when that will occur. But you can be assured that those decisions will be forthcoming shortly. And with reference to the issue regarding the compensation for your legal advisors, I emphasise again, Mr. Tolimir, that it is your election to be self-represented, and that of course has an impact on the scale and on the nature of the legal advisors that you can engage and the scale range for them. But most significantly, that is a matter which rests in the hands of the Registrar; and I understand that they have been in discussion with you on those compensation issues and have been demonstrating flexibility from their guide-lines. And the Trial Chamber will only intervene if there is a particular decision of the Registrar that is brought to our attention. We will of course consider any motions that you file in that respect, but the primary, the first, stop with regard to those issues is with the Registry. And I encourage you to continue your dialogue with them regarding the compensation issues. And as I say, the Trial Chamber will maintain its oversight responsibilities and your -- you can certainly bring to our attention, as you have, any particular issues you wish us to consider. So that will be the position of the Trial Chamber with regard to that matter. So if that then covers, I believe, the issues related to trial preparations, the other matter, Mr. Tolimir, that I want to raise in accordance with the Rules is the issue of whether you have any questions or issues that you wish to bring to my attention, to the Chamber's attention, regarding your health or your treatment at the UNDU. As has been the practice per your request, we will stay in open session for any of those issues unless you advise me otherwise. But are there any matters you wish to bring to my attention, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise for going back to the previous question by your leave. I am not asking that my legal assistants receive anything that they are not entitled to. I want them to be compensated because the pre-trial stage has been extended in relation to the initial ones. I have already sent my motion to the Registry, and in that sense I ask for your assistance in order to explain the Registrar that the pre-trial period was extended because the OTP filed additional material. And as for the remainder of the session, I want to remain in open session, as always. If I may continue. As you know, I have not received any treatment with medication since my arrival here. I mostly treat myself with food and with various teas, and I think that you're quite aware of that. I think that doctors, experts of the Defence and experts of the Registry, have already given their opinion, whereby they said that given my current condition it's not necessary for me to be disturbed every half an hour and to be waken up to given treatment. Now, if it's not sufficient for the Trial Chamber that these two experts engaged by me and engaged by Registrar saying that I do not need to be disturbed and I'm still disturbed at night, I wonder whether that is done pursuant to the order of the Chamber. I don't think that that needs to be done. Perhaps I need to be examined every six months, that should be enough. They measure my blood pressure. They saw that my blood pressure was 130 over 80, and I don't see any reason why I should be disturbed every 30 minutes. I think you would not like it if somebody opened your office, opened your window, or did something similar that that would disturb you that would cause you to lose concentration and so on. So I think you can understand how I feel when they do that to me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Yes, reverting to the issue -- I understand your point regarding the extension of the pre-trial period, and I'm confident that the matter will be taken into consideration by the Registrar. And it's now noted on the record, so I'm sure that will be the case. Now, regarding the issue of sleep disturbance, which as you know, Mr. Tolimir, I and the Chamber have taken very seriously since you have raised this issue. As I made clear, though, at the last Status Conference, based on the medical reports that the Trial Chamber will rely on, the position was that provided you were prepared to co-operate both in terms of having your blood pressure checked and in terms of medication, only in those circumstances as recommended by the medical experts would the Trial Chamber intervene specifically with the Registrar. Now, you have expressed your position very clearly that you do not wish to take the medication which has been recommended by all of the medical experts that have examined you and your records; and obviously that is your choice. But in those circumstances, the Chamber leaves the matter in the hands of the UNDU and the medical staff there to determine, based on all the material that's been provided to them, as to the necessity for the nightly checks on you. I understand that Dr. Folke has been in discussion with you about this. I requested that a second review be given to the matter after the last Status Conference, that he take a look at all the material that's been filed, and I understand that he is working with you to perhaps try and reduce those checks. And I and the Chamber will leave that matter in the hands of the UNDU unless we are advised that you have agreed to both the conditions set by the medical experts, in which case then we will ask the appropriate authorities at the UNDU to cease the checks. But I think that position is very clear from what I stated at the last conference, and I'm clarifying it again. I understand your difficulties with the checks, but the Chamber must be guided by the medical information that we have before us, and we will continue to be guided. We will, however, continue to monitor the situation, and as I say, I have raised it with the Registrar and Dr. Folke has followed up on the questions that I put forward. So that's where the situation stands. It is again, though, Mr. Tolimir, in your hands in terms of your decisions as to medical treatment. If there is nothing further that you wish to raise, Mr. Tolimir -- yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that the opinion of the doctor, the specialist, engaged by the Registrar was not presented appropriately, accurately. He said in his report that given my current condition there is no need to conduct these checks on Tolimir and that Tolimir is only recommended one medication, aspirin, by Bayer. It is a medication produced in Serbia. He said that -- he did not say that I have to take any medication. If you wish to conduct checks on me, of course you can do that, but I wish to inform you as the Presiding Judge that I cannot work normally with all these disturbances. If somebody disturbs your work every half an hour, you couldn't work either. Not a single expert or doctor said that I am under these checks because I refused to take medication. I treat myself with various herbal teas. So it's not that I am without treatment. I can either choose to treat myself with medication or with herbs, which is what I'm doing. And I don't see why they are blackmailing me. They are blackmailing he me so that I will take medication. What I request is that I be left to work without any disturbances and that I -- that these checks be discontinued. I want to be told what results were achieved as a result of this treatment that has lasted for two years. If you wish me to undergo this further, then it's all right, I will. But please make a ruling so that I can ask for certification to appeal that ruling. My current medical condition is not such that -- as to require such checks. Therefore, I don't know who else I can turn to. I can turn to you, I can turn to the Appeals Chamber. Therefore, I ask for you to review once again the entire situation with all the facts that I've presented to you and to make a final ruling. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. I think you've made your position on this very clear, and I believe the Chamber's position on this is very clear as well. I will once again, however, discuss the matter with the Registry, as I do. And we will keep the matter on -- within our agenda, but I don't believe we can advance further with it today. So I understand your perspective. I will take on board the comments that you have made, and I will continue to keep the matter under consideration. I believe that those were all of the matters that I had on the agenda for today. Are there any additional matters, because the next meeting will be obviously at the start of the trial. I perhaps can provide just a bit more information in that regard. As you know from the decision of the Chamber, the trial has been delayed from the date of the decision for at least a two-month period. So we're looking at mid-February for -- at the earliest for a start date. Because there are many variables that fit into the question of the actual start date, I'm not in a position to provide any more specific information on that today. Obviously the motions and other matters will have to be considered with respect to that, but the Trial Chamber will be issuing a Scheduling Order as soon as is feasible in light of the new circumstances. So that's the best of the information I can provide for today. But I would anticipate that the next gathering will be for the Pre-Trial Conference. Anything further, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, anything further?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then I wish everyone a good afternoon and the Status Conference is adjourned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.49 p.m.
